key_insight: A store-level reinforcement learning policy learns a discrete dispatch weight multiplier from delayed marketplace feedback to improve batching and courier efficiency while preserving delivery quality.
engineering_relevance: The system shows how to safely deploy offline RL inside a production optimizer by adjusting objective weights instead of replacing the combinatorial assignment engine.
method: Train a shared value function from centralized offline marketplace logs.
Use Double Q-learning with a conservative regularizer to curb out-of-distribution value overestimation.
Execute a decentralized store-level policy that selects a discrete multiplier for the dispatch optimizer tradeoff.
evidence_signal: In a production switchback experiment, the offline-trained policy increased batching and reduced courier-side time costs without degrading customer-facing delivery quality.
watch_item: Because feedback is delayed and coupled across merchants, couriers, and customers, offline value estimation and production safeguards must be carefully managed to avoid unsafe policy shifts.
paper_title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Marketplace Feedback for Objective-Weight Adaptation in Three-Sided Dispatch
